findings.observation: Native SetCollider repeats NullReferenceException after same-room reconnect. Supplemental trace identifies Control/Throw and Throw Recover with missing Needle Tink target.
findings.resolution: Reference initialization erased still-live detached child targets; reconnect activation restarted already-running root FSMs and cleared their variables; resumed rigidbody entities could also lack velocity/gravity snapshots. Shared initialization now preserves valid detached references, rebinds available hierarchy matches before activation/state recovery, temporarily preserves started native root FSM state, and restores initial velocity/gravity through existing components.
findings.verificationScope: Both first-entry orders completed six real needle-throw disconnect/reconnect cycles with natural Throw Recover, live Needle/Tink references, common boss identity/health, visible peers and clean strict logs. findings.finalVerificationScope: Both entry orders passed actual native moving A Dash restoration, all static identities, six real throw/recover reconnect cycles, native/replica tween cloning and clean strict logs on production build 6ddf5b3. Full twelve-case suite remains independently required.

findings.observation: Fifth guest-first throw reconnect preserved Needle/Tink references but Hornet stayed in Thrown and never reached Throw Recover. Host registered Needle as 4568293017055036489 beneath Hornet; guest registered its detached Needle as 6622943944039214165 at scene root.
findings.cause: Static entity IDs were recomputed from the current hierarchy on same-scene reconnect, after the previous connection's detached-part bindings were cleared. Native reparenting and dormant replicas can have different paths.
findings.correction: A native object lifetime now retains its first static identity in metadata that survives network disconnect. Copied metadata validates object instance and scene; dynamic pooled lifetimes retain their independent IDs.
findings.releaseRequirement: Baseline identity assertion must fail on the previous build; modified build must retain common static IDs and naturally throw/recover through six reconnect cycles in both entry orders, followed by all twelve final-hash acceptance cases.
findings.finalVerificationScope: Both entry orders passed actual native moving A Dash restoration, all static identities, six real throw/recover reconnect cycles, native/replica tween cloning and clean strict logs on production build 6ddf5b3. Full twelve-case suite remains independently required.

findings.observation: Guest-first Grimm acceptance lost both connections; host Unity log contains GoToProfileMenu failures and a native access violation. The crash report is preserved privately. Gameplay probes directly called Connect with autoConnect false even after selecting an in-memory character, allowing an asynchronous save menu to race scene entry.
findings.correction: Gameplay-only fixtures now retain their already-selected character. The menu/new-save JoinProbe continues using the real selection path. Observe actual profile-menu requests and reject them in the Grimm gameplay probe; native crash signatures independently reject the release log gate.

findings.observation: Final host-first lifecycle run passed the natural dash and first needle recovery, but replica activation during a reconnect snapshot raised iTween.RetrieveArgs/Awake NullReferenceException through Entity.UpdateIsActive.
findings.cause: Instantiating a currently tweening native hierarchy copies runtime iTween components. Their nonserialized arguments remain in a global table targeted at the original object; the inactive clone's first Awake cannot retrieve its own arguments.
findings.correction: Remove copied runtime iTween components immediately from the inactive clone hierarchy before its first activation. Do not Stop copied IDs or modify the native global arguments. Fresh network-driven replica animations may still create new tweens normally.
findings.releaseRequirement: The actual production cloning fixture must fail on the old engine and pass with native root/child tween arguments intact and fresh replica animation verified. Both six-cycle lifecycle orders and all twelve final-hash cases must pass clean strict logs.
findings.finalVerificationScope: Both entry orders passed actual native moving A Dash restoration, all static identities, six real throw/recover reconnect cycles, native/replica tween cloning and clean strict logs on production build 6ddf5b3. Full twelve-case suite remains independently required.

findings.observation: Static identities matched, but the initial same-room reconnect left native Hornet in A Dash for 100 seconds. A targeted natural-dash baseline recorded velocity (-23.5,-18.7) before disconnect and (0,0) after re-registering the same native authority, with A Dash unchanged and no natural completion.
findings.cause: Native hierarchy deactivation clears body velocity. New entity components on same-scene registration have no received network snapshot to restore it. Preserving FSM state alone therefore resumes a motion-dependent state at zero velocity.
findings.correction: Capture active rigidbodies before pausing the parent and restore them after all managed children initialize as authority. Discard local paused motion for replicas/takeover. A changed native FSM state takes precedence over paused physics.
findings.releaseRequirement: Both final lifecycle cases must select a real moving native A Dash, reconnect its existing authority first, observe motion and natural completion, and complete six needle reconnect cycles. All twelve final-hash runtime cases remain required.
findings.finalVerificationScope: Both entry orders passed actual native moving A Dash restoration, all static identities, six real throw/recover reconnect cycles, native/replica tween cloning and clean strict logs on production build 6ddf5b3. Full twelve-case suite remains independently required.
